reading.body:
QTS Chicago is a planned two-building campus on 30 acres near downtown Chicago with closed-loop water-recirculating cooling, LEED Gold and Energy Star certified for efficient operations. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity or square footage figures for this facility. Without published IT load or building size, the campus's relevance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from available data.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities, of which only 6 publish capacity figures totaling 236 MW. QTS Chicago is ranked seventh in the state by published capacity, which means it either publishes no figures and ranks below all six disclosed sites, or the ranking reflects planned or announced capacity not yet confirmed in published specifications. The state's published capacity is modest by national AI infrastructure standards.

The facility's two-building structure and water cooling systems indicate capability for dense compute, but the absence of published power or space specifications makes it impossible to determine whether this campus will serve as a meaningful hub for AI workloads or remain a regional colocation provider. Future disclosure of IT load or occupancy would clarify its role.
